items.context: WuBlockchain: Ledger confirma hardware wallets alteradas físicamente (ataque a la cadena de suministro) en Berlín; dos equipos sospechosos en Dubái siguen en investigación. Noticia fresca de custodia con 24 likes y solo 16 respuestas, sin respuesta de @ForecastQuant.
items.suggested_text:
The uncomfortable part of this story isn't Ledger specifically. It's that "bought from an authorized retailer" is no longer a guarantee. A supply-chain attack doesn't need to break the secure element; it only needs to sit between the factory and you long enough to modify the hardware or plant a seed you didn't generate.

That's why the setup ritual matters more than the brand: create the seed yourself on the device, never accept a pre-printed one, run the genuine/attestation check, and test a recovery before sending real funds. Keeping the signing device air-gapped adds another layer, because a compromised unit with no path to the network has a much harder time leaking anything.

Most of these losses are decided in the first minutes of setup, not years later. Few people treat those minutes as the part that actually matters.
